The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's own GitHub repository using a tagged release archive over HTTPS. There are no command substitutions, remote code executions, or network operations in the global scope or in the `pkgver()` function (which is absent and thus defaults to the static `pkgver` value). The sourcing of this PKGBUILD during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` or `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will not trigger execution of any untrusted or dynamically fetched code. All variables and functions are declarative or used in later build stages that are skipped by these flags.

Standard AUR practices are followed: the source is pinned to a version tag, checksummed, and uses a direct archival link. No `pkgver()` function is present, so no dynamic version calculation occurs that could hide malicious logic. The top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments. Therefore, running the specified makepkg commands poses no risk of unintended code execution or data exfiltration.
</details>
